# Bloxwap HIG 0.1.0 candidate

## ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts
Source: docs/architecture/001-packages.md

# ADR 001: platform renderers, shared contracts

Status: accepted for candidate 0.1.0. Issues #4, #5. Evidence: `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Tokens[HIG tokens] --> Web[HIG React]
  Tokens --> Native[HIG Native]
  Contracts[HIG contracts] --> Web
  Contracts --> Native
  Contracts --> Feedback[optional feedback adapters]
  Web --> Docs[docs and consumer fixtures]
  Native --> Expo[Expo gallery]
```

`@bloxwap/hig-tokens` owns palette, density, units and generation; `@bloxwap/hig-contracts` owns platform-neutral types and formatting. `@bloxwap/hig-react` and `@bloxwap/hig-native` own renderers. `@bloxwap/hig-chart` owns the web adapter for `@bloxwap/chart` (`PriceChart`, `chartTheme`), with `@bloxwap/chart` and `@bloxwap/hig-react` as required peers (#96). No other package names `@bloxwap/chart`: an optional peer on it made npm 11 drop chart's workspace copy when that repository regenerated its lockfile. `@bloxwap/hig-feedback` owns optional adapter entry points. `@bloxwap/hig-native-fonts` ships the static native TTFs (#64), and `@bloxwap/hig-og-fonts` ships the five byte-identical Latin faces that Satori/`next/og` cards need (#99). Both are generated from pinned `@bloxwap/font` sources by `npm run generate:fonts`, and they are the only packages allowed to contain font binaries. Base controls never load audio, haptics, charts, Expo or another platform. Each component has an individual export; CSS is explicit and side-effectful. Plain HTML consumers use tokens/CSS alone.

Candidate validation matrix: Node 22.22+, TypeScript 5.9, React/DOM 19.1, RN 0.81.5 with Expo 54 and RN 0.83.10 with Expo 55 (React 19.1.0 and 19.2.0 respectively, #68), Vite 6.4. Next 16.4.0 webpack is verified by M5 production/packed consumer checks. NativeWind styling remains outside the supported StyleSheet consumer path. Use StyleSheet on RN and plain CSS on web; Tailwind may refer to `var(--hig-*)` without scanning HIG sources. The pinned monorepo source now documents web/native rem roots of 16; see source reconciliation. Never infer native sizes by replacing `rem` with `dp`.

Prefer built-in semantic controls; modal/disclosure behavior must retain keyboard, focus restoration and descriptions. The separate `@bloxwap/hig-chart` package imports the chart SDK only on the client. Libraries retain upstream licenses; extracted tokens and mark have commit provenance, no vendor engine source is copied. Font binaries remain owned by @bloxwap/font (OFL-1.1).

Deprecation plan: inventory all live references, map variants to intent/density, run migration diff and consumer validation, switch a pilot behind a host flag, then delete unused copies. App comfortable targets and Pro compact rows are intentional. HIG cannot retire owning-repository copies within this hig-only change. API/token/behavior changes follow semver; breaking accessibility behavior counts as breaking. Support upgrades require web, SSR and Metro evidence with a documented rollback before changing the matrix.


## Attribution and provenance
Source: docs/architecture/attribution.md

# Attribution and provenance

HIG code: MIT. @radix-ui/react-dialog, dropdown-menu, popover, tooltip: MIT, consumed as dependencies without copied engine code. @bloxwap/chart/sfx/haptic: independent upstream packages; optional integration only (chart through the separate `@bloxwap/hig-chart` adapter). @bloxwap/font: OFL-1.1, binaries stay in its pinned package. Brand SVG/geometry derives from Font docs, exact upstream commit in `evidence/upstream-inventory.json`; do not imply arbitrary trademark relicensing. Utility CheckIcon is original simple geometry. Full icons catalogs are excluded.

## Generated favicon and social preview

`npm run generate` derives unchanged SVG favicons and a 1200×630 SVG social preview from the approved mark. Source SHA256 and derivative paths are in `planning/brand-artifacts.json`; lint rejects stale outputs. The derived preview declares its lineage and omits the source credential metadata; unchanged source/favicons retain it. Hosts whose social crawlers require raster images must render a PNG from this same SVG instead of redrawing the mark. This preview uses a generic font rather than embedding the full font asset.


## Candidate platform support · 0.1.0
Source: docs/architecture/platform-matrix.md

# Candidate platform support · 0.1.0

| Area | DOM | RN | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Actions, surfaces, text, fields | Semantic DOM elements | Pressable/View/Text/TextInput | behavior tests, Vite/SSR/Metro |
| Native text scaling and script tracking | Browser zoom; no cap | `Text`/`Heading`/`NumberReadout` `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (prop or HIGProvider default); Korean/Chinese runs at companion spacing via `script` and `letterSpacingByScript` | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator AX5: capped readout 48pt vs 86pt prose; Android emulator 200% (non-linear scaling stays under the 2x cap) (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Native colour roles | CSS severity/data attributes | `Switch` `tone`, `Alert` `severity`/`tone` take token roles only; raw colours fall back. The Android Switch thumb uses the `text` token instead of the app theme accent | native Jest (#67); iOS Simulator and Android emulator captures (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Native colour space | CSS sRGB with P3 in `@supports` | `HIGProvider colorSpace` `srgb` (default) or `display-p3`; every component paints from `useColors()`; iOS `display-p3` uses `nativeColors.iosDisplayP3`, Android and web stay sRGB; no raw colours | native Jest (#93: P3 values for action/warning/negative/info, direct-import guard); iOS Simulator capture as a Display P3 host (`evidence/native-sim/issue-93/`); physical display pending (#55) |
| Selection/range | Built-in input/select | OS Switch/community Slider, radio/check Pressables, Modal chooser; Android Slider adds `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` through the autolinked `HIGAdjustableView` (plain View without native linking) | contract tests; Android emulator UiAutomation (#71): set-progress listed, 80 applied once, snapped/clamped, absent and rejected while disabled; iOS Simulator increment/decrement unchanged (`evidence/native-sim/issue-67-71/`) |
| Dialog/sheet/menu | Radix scoped primitives; optional Vaul GestureSheet entry | Modal and explicit close/back; optional Gorhom GestureSheet entry | DOM nested focus/Escape plus real Chromium/WebKit sheet drag, scroll and snap checks; mocked native focus/back/detents plus separate packed Android/iOS gesture entry |
| Tooltip/popover | Radix hover/focus/anchored | persistent HelpText/modal | no RN hover claim |
| Navigation/search | href/callback adapters | host route/back callbacks | tab/search/disclosure contracts |
| Financial lists/table | semantic table/list | FlatList labeled rows | formatting and contract tests |
| Chart | `@bloxwap/hig-chart`: lazy @bloxwap/chart canvas (required peer) | numeric/list summary only | typed theme; physical gesture evidence pending |
| Brand mark | individual SVG renderer/asset | optional react-native-svg | pinned geometry; device comparison pending |
| React Native versions | — | RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 / React 19.1.0 and RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55 / React 19.2.0; peer ranges `react-native` `^0.81.5 \|\| ^0.83.10`, SDK-matched Expo, SVG, Slider and Worklets peers | CI packed Metro exports for both (`smoke:packed-native`, `--profile rn-0.83`); iOS Simulator and Android emulator gallery, interaction and GestureSheet runs on both with the same outcomes; differences tracked in #86–#89 (`evidence/native-sim/rn-0.83/`) |
| Fonts | pinned Sans/Mono asset URLs | hash-pinned static faces, typed manifest, explicit weight registration and host script fallback | Expo-web loading/byte/hash gates; no physical native-font certification |

SSR: client components retain use-client boundaries in emitted JS. Importing a button needs React/tokens/contracts only at runtime. CSS is explicitly imported. Native API never imports DOM, Web Audio or chart. Native target size remains comfortable even when host density is compact; Pro density is a DOM exception, not a reason to shrink phone targets.

Optional peer packages: none for chart, whose adapter is the separate `@bloxwap/hig-chart` package with a required `@bloxwap/chart` peer (#96); community Slider for native selection entry; react-native-svg for native brand entry. Vaul is isolated behind the web gesture-sheet entry; Gorhom/Reanimated/Worklets/Gesture Handler are isolated behind the native gesture-sheet entry. Base imports do not load them. No root barrel loads every component. DOM overlays are one scoped family entry and carry Radix MIT attribution; Radix peers are optional caret ranges and overlay-free web recipes have their own entries. ESM is supported; CommonJS consumer support is not claimed.


## CI runners · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/ci-runners.md

# CI runners · HIG 0.1.0

Every GitHub Actions job in this repository runs on self-hosted Apple silicon Mac minis:

```yaml
runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
```

There are no GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` jobs. Workflows do not call `apt`, `sudo`, or Playwright `--with-deps`. Scratch directories use `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Jobs that run npm/Python/Playwright export `TMPDIR=$RUNNER_TEMP` through `GITHUB_ENV` (the `runner` context is not available in workflow or job `env`).

## Required on every runner

- macOS on Apple silicon, with the Actions runner registered using the labels `self-hosted`, `macOS`, and `ARM64`
- Git
- Python 3.10+ with the standard-library `venv` module (`fonttools` 4.61.1 requires `>=3.10`). GitHub's `actions/setup-python` macOS builds mkdir `/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache` and fail on these minis (`Permission denied`). CI therefore installs relocatable CPython 3.12 into `$RUNNER_TEMP` with a pinned `uv` 0.13.1 binary (`scripts/ci-setup-python.sh`). The login-shell Python does not have to be 3.12. Cache misses create `$RUNNER_TEMP/hig-fonttools` and install `fonttools[woff]==4.61.1` and `brotli==1.2.0` there; they do not write to system site-packages
- Network access to npm, GitHub, and Playwright browser downloads
- Homebrew `gnu-tar` on **every** mini so `gtar` is on the runner service `PATH` or at `$(brew --prefix)/opt/gnu-tar/bin`. `actions/upload-pages-artifact` invokes `gtar` on macOS (`--hard-dereference` is a GNU option). Install with `brew install gnu-tar`. One machine having it is not enough.
- Disk for npm caches, Playwright browsers at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`, packed-consumer trees under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and generated font faces

Node 22.22.0 is installed per job by `actions/setup-node`. It does not need to be the login-shell default.

## Playwright

Jobs that need browsers run `npx playwright install chromium webkit` with no `--with-deps`. Browsers stay on disk at `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` across jobs on a mini; do not save that folder with `actions/cache` (it stalls 11+ minutes because the directory is shared). Chromium and WebKit must launch headless as the runner user. Playwright Firefox is not installed or launched.

## Visual baselines

Catalog Button/Field/Input states and Slider focus captures live under `tests/visual-baselines/<process.platform>/` (`linux` or `darwin`). Geometry changes still fail; pixel changes still fail above 2% after a 24-channel-value antialias tolerance. Missing Darwin images fail closed: review the uploaded capture and commit it with `HIG_UPDATE_VISUALS=1`. Do not copy a Linux baseline or raise the thresholds to hide an OS difference.

## Not required for these workflows

The `native` job exports Android and iOS Metro bundles (`smoke:packed-native` for RN 0.81.5 / Expo 54 and RN 0.83.10 / Expo 55). It does not boot simulators. Xcode, an iOS Simulator runtime, JDK 17, and the Android SDK are only for local `scripts/native-sim/` gallery runs, which these workflows do not execute.

## Jobs

### HIG candidate quality and dry-run artifacts (`quality.yml`)

| Job | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `paths-filter` | Same PR path filter as before; docs-only PRs skip the heavy jobs |
| `quality` | `check`, examples, quality gates, SSR and packed smokes, Playwright packed-next/css, release dry-run |
| `native` | Packed native Metro export for both supported RN/Expo profiles |
| `browser` | Chromium and WebKit browser, visual, and hydration gates |
| `candidate` | Aggregator so the required check reports on docs-only PRs |

### Documentation (`docs.yml`)

| Job | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `build` | Static docs build, typecheck, GitHub Pages artifact |
| `deploy` | GitHub Pages deploy from `main` |


## Actions & surfaces · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/actions-surfaces.md

# Actions & surfaces · HIG 0.1.0

Buttons, typography, and layout primitives for clear actions and related content.

Includes `Button`, `IconButton`, `Link`, `Text`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card`, and `Separator`.

Issue #13. Entry: `button / surface`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/button` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/button` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Button`, `IconButton` | `children`, `intent`, `busy`, `busyLabel`, `disabled`, `fullWidth`, `suppressFeedback`, and forwarded ref. Web uses `onClick`; native uses `onPress`. The busy suffix (` · Working`) comes from HIGProvider `messages.busy` or `busyLabel`; `''` hides it while busy state stays exposed. Native: the label and suffix render through HIG `Text` (HIGProvider or `maxFontSizeMultiplier` prop font-scale cap, registered family for the weight, per-script letter spacing), and a busy Button with text children sets its accessible name ([localization rule](../foundations/localization.md#built-in-component-strings)); an explicit `accessibilityLabel` wins. |
| `Link` | Platform link behavior; host applications own routing. |
| `Text`, `Heading` | Platform text props. Native adds `maxFontSizeMultiplier` (font-scale cap for dense numeric readouts, also on `NumberReadout`; HIGProvider sets a default) and `script` (`latin`, `ko`, `zh`; detected from string children). Korean and Chinese runs use the companion face's own spacing (`scriptLetterSpacing`, 0em) instead of Latin tracking; HIGProvider `letterSpacingByScript` overrides it per script in em. |
| `Stack`, `Inline`, `Surface`, `Card` | Platform layout props. |

## When to use and examples

Use one primary review action. Do: busy protects host requests and displays the translated busy label (`Working` in English). Don’t: use destructive red for every sell button.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM semantic button/anchor, forwarded focus, target min-height tied to density (web: 44px comfortable, 36px compact); RN target always at least 48. Multiline labels wrap; RN custom children render in a View with text nodes styled individually.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN external Link uses Linking; routes belong to host. Native fontFamily only after registration. Decorative SVG hidden; IconButton label is mandatory.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Charts · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/chart.md

# Charts · HIG 0.1.0

Web price charts with text summaries and native readout alternatives.

Includes web-only `PriceChart` and `chartTheme`. Native uses readouts, lists, and text summaries.

Issues #20 and #96. Package: `@bloxwap/hig-chart`. Import `PriceChart` and `chartTheme` from `@bloxwap/hig-chart` for the DOM canvas integration only. Native consumers use `@bloxwap/hig-native/data` for summary/readout/list alternatives. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

```sh
npm install @bloxwap/hig-chart @bloxwap/hig-react @bloxwap/chart@^0.3.0
```

`@bloxwap/hig-chart` has three required peers: `react`, `@bloxwap/hig-react` (its `HIGProvider` supplies the localized fallback) and `@bloxwap/chart` `^0.3.0`. Its dependencies are `@bloxwap/hig-tokens` and `@bloxwap/hig-contracts`. `@bloxwap/hig-react` itself declares no `@bloxwap/chart` peer and has no `./chart` entry.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `PriceChart` | `data`, required `summary`, `height`, and chart SDK props. |
| `chartTheme` | Token-based colors in sRGB for canvas compatibility. |

## When to use and examples

Do: provide host-generated price/trend summary and lazy-load chart on demand. Don’t: play effects on ticks or present web canvas as RN.

## States, interaction and accessibility

@bloxwap/chart/react loads only on PriceChart render, in Suspense. Token theme covers surface/text/border/grid/crosshair/up/down/fonts; engine owns gestures and cleanup.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Moved from `@bloxwap/hig-react/chart` (#96)

Until #96 the adapter was the `./chart` entry of `@bloxwap/hig-react`, which declared `@bloxwap/chart` as an optional peer. npm 11.6 drops a workspace copy of `@bloxwap/chart` from a lockfile regenerated from scratch without `legacy-peer-deps` whenever an installed package declares it as an optional peer. bloxwap/chart hit this: its `packages/chart` workspace disappeared and `apps/docs` lost `@bloxwap/chart`. Repacking hig-react without that peer kept the link. A required peer on a separate package does not trigger it, so the adapter moved to `@bloxwap/hig-chart` and the peer is required there. `npm run smoke:packed-chart-workspace` builds a chart-shaped workspace and regenerates its lockfile from scratch with strict peers, under both the ambient npm and the pinned npm 11.6.1. It fails if the link is lost (see the release chapter).

Migration: replace `@bloxwap/hig-react/chart` with `@bloxwap/hig-chart` in imports and add `@bloxwap/hig-chart` next to `@bloxwap/hig-react`. `PriceChart` props and `chartTheme` values are unchanged.

```diff
-import {PriceChart, chartTheme} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/chart';
+import {PriceChart, chartTheme} from '@bloxwap/hig-chart';
```

Consumers: an org-wide GitHub code search (default branches) on 2026-10-16 found no import of `@bloxwap/hig-react/chart` outside this repository. bloxwap/chart, sfx and haptic import only other hig-react entries, and chart builds its own theme from `@bloxwap/hig-tokens`. The candidate was never published. The release chapter normally keeps a deprecated export working for a minor release, but that is skipped here: there are no consumers to migrate, and a working shim would need the optional peer that causes the bug. Hosts that only use other hig-react entries change nothing. bloxwap/chart can drop the `legacy-peer-deps` regeneration note in `vendor/bloxwap-hig/README.md` at its next HIG refresh.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN canvas is unsupported in this candidate. Use NumberReadout/List plus host summaries. A native chart engine/WebView bridge needs a separate supported target and device lifecycle review, rather than an invented integration.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Fields & inputs · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/fields.md

# Fields & inputs · HIG 0.1.0

Labeled inputs for text, search, and amounts, with visible help and validation.

Includes `Field`, `Label`, `Input`, `TextArea`, `AmountInput`, and `SearchInput`.

Issue #14. Entry: `field`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/field` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/field` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Field` | `label`, `id` (web), `description`, `error`, `required`, and `disabled`. |
| `Input`, `TextArea` | Platform input props and forwarded refs. |
| `AmountInput` | Text input with decimal keyboard hints; `value` stays a raw string. |

## When to use and examples

Do: label Amount (BTC), describe available funds, keep 0,001 unchanged until host validates locale. Don’t: placeholder-only labels, Number(raw) on every keystroke, or strip IME text.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Single-line inputs are 48-unit pills on the surface fill with a subtle border; focus thickens the border to a neutral ring and invalid inputs take the negative border. TextArea keeps a rounded rectangle. DOM label/id plus help/error aria-describedby; invalid state is explicit. Field required propagates to Input/TextArea for browser required semantics and form validation; explicit input props can override required. A disabled Field keeps its controls disabled even if a child requests otherwise. Native amount keyboardType and search returnKeyType remain host-overridable defaults for locale/negative-entry and submit flows. RN visible label plus accessibilityLabel/Hint; errors stay visible and live. Secure input and autofill remain host-controlled native props.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

RN decimal-pad has locale/platform differences; no implicit money parser. Host owns safe area and keyboard avoidance: on Android 15 edge-to-edge (Expo 54) the window no longer resizes for the IME, so wrap scrollable forms in `KeyboardAvoidingView behavior='padding'` on Android and use `automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets` on the iOS ScrollView, as the native gallery does. iOS Simulator and Android emulator runs show the AmountInput decimal pad and the focused field kept above the keyboard (`evidence/native-sim/`); physical IME composition and hardware-keyboard behavior remain device observations.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Financial data · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/financial-data.md

# Financial data · HIG 0.1.0

Readable numbers, metrics, lists, and tables for host-provided financial data.

Includes `NumberReadout`, `AnimatedNumberReadout`, `Usd`, `Percent`, `Metric`, `Stat`, `Row`, and `List`. `Table` is web-only; native uses labeled lists.

Issue #19. Entry: `data`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/data` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/data` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Readouts | `value` accepts a number, `null`, or `undefined`. Locale comes from the provider; `options`, `stale`, and `label` control presentation. |
| `List` | `items`, `keyFor`, `render`, `empty`, `label`, `loading`, `error`, `onRetry`, and `onLoadMore`. |
| `Table` (web) | `caption`, `rows`, `columns`, and `keyFor`; optional host sorting callbacks. Column `align` accepts logical `start`, `center`, or `end`. `rowProps(row, index)` forwards row highlights, styles, data/ARIA attributes and events. `captionHidden`, `stickyHeader`, `loading`, and `state` support dense product tables. |

Loading keeps existing rows visible, suppresses a misleading empty message, and disables pagination and retry until ready. Error text remains visible with an optional host retry action. Native lists use FlatList virtualization; stable host keys preserve identity during live updates.

Native readouts, including `Usd`, `Percent`, and `AnimatedNumberReadout`, accept `tone="text" | "positive" | "negative" | "muted"`, `testID`, and a constrained typography `style`. The style accepts `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, and `textAlign`, including registered styles and arrays. The tone resolves through the provider palette; it is explicit rather than inferred from the sign. Colour and tabular numeric glyphs stay controlled by the readout. Font scale follows HIG Text and the provider; `maxFontSizeMultiplier` can override its cap.

For a branded 20 px equity pill, use `<NumberReadout value={equity} label="Equity" testID="equity" style={{fontFamily:'BloxwapMonoSemiBold',fontSize:20,lineHeight:28}} />` with a registered host font. For signed PnL, add `tone={pnl < 0 ? 'negative' : 'positive'}` and `options={{signDisplay:'always'}}`. The same props on `AnimatedNumberReadout` style and identify the final text reading; opacity motion stays on its wrapper.

Native readouts also accept `formattedValue` for a host's existing static display format, such as `<NumberReadout value={90} formattedValue="01:30" label="Time remaining" />`. The host owns this opaque display text and its localization; never parse it for submission or calculations. A finite numeric `value` is still required: `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`, and infinities display the canonical unknown dash even if text is supplied. An empty string falls back to the usual locale and `options` formatting. Stale text, the accessible label, semantic tone, and tabular typography still apply to the resulting reading. Existing moving digit reels need an explicit motion decision before switching to a static readout.

Web tables keep a visible caption and ordinary headers by default. Set `captionHidden` when a visible section already names the table: the caption remains its accessible name. `stickyHeader` pins header cells within a bounded scroll region; give the region a height through `style` or `className`. `tableClassName` styles the table itself. Sorting still belongs to the host, and sort buttons retain native keyboard activation and `aria-sort`.

```tsx
<Table caption='Positions' captionHidden stickyHeader style={{maxHeight:320}}
  rows={positions} keyFor={row=>row.id}
  rowProps={row=>({className:row.current?'current-market':undefined,'aria-current':row.current?'true':undefined})}
  columns={[
    {key:'market',label:'Market',render:row=>row.symbol},
    {key:'balance',label:'Balance',align:'end',render:row=><NumberReadout value={row.balance}/>},
  ]}
  loading={refreshing}
  state={error?<div role='alert'>{error}<button type='button' onClick={retry}>Retry</button></div>:undefined}/>
```

The `state` slot is content for one cell spanning all columns; it can contain an empty explanation, loading skeleton, or error and retry UI. Pass content rather than `tr`/`td` elements. Existing data rows remain visible. Without a custom state, `loading` exposes the provider's `loading` message and `aria-busy`; an empty, idle table shows `noRows`. `state={null}` suppresses that fallback. Give custom errors an alert role and custom loading content a status role when an announcement is appropriate. `rowProps` cannot replace the row's native role or HIG's cells with `children`/HTML. Row callbacks do not add a selection keyboard model; use native controls inside cells for actions.

## When to use and examples

Do: show — for unknown and 0 for zero; mark stale. Don’t: turn a formatted number into order quantity or announce every live tick. Locale display, USD vs USDC, signed PnL and compact notation follow the [localization guide](../foundations/localization.md). Vocabulary follows the [glossary](../foundations/glossary.md).

## States, interaction and accessibility

Readouts are static and tabular, respecting reduced motion. Percent uses percent points (5 is 5%), with localized percent placement/digits and a single native text readout. Intl options control precision/trailing zeros/sign; percent style is enforced. Unknown/nonfinite values stay —. DOM table caption/column headers/aria-sort and scroll region; RN FlatList labeled-row alternative with stable keys.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Numbers are display-only IEEE numeric inputs, no decimal arithmetic or hidden parser. Exact financial strings remain host-owned. No heavy DataTable engine; optional virtualization/sorting belongs to host. Native list device performance pending.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/pro-data.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/pro-data-typecheck.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

## Optional number motion

`AnimatedNumberReadout` lives in the separate `animated-number` entry on both platforms. It fades the final localized reading on a deliberate value change, using Web Animations or the RN native opacity driver. It never interpolates financial values or adds a live region. Reduced motion, unknown values and changes less than 250 ms apart use the static final reading; pending motion is canceled on replacement/unmount. No animation engine is imported by the ordinary `data` entry. Example: `import {AnimatedNumberReadout} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/animated-number'` (or `hig-native/animated-number`), then `<AnimatedNumberReadout value={price} label="Price" options={{style:'currency',currency:'USD'}} />`. The same gallery manifest contains runnable examples for both renderers.


## Navigation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/navigation.md

# Navigation · HIG 0.1.0

Tabs, disclosure, search, and navigation that keep the current location clear.

Includes `Tabs`, `Accordion`, `Pagination`, `Navigation`, and `Search`. `Breadcrumb` is web-only; native alternatives include `BackButton` and `BottomNavigation`.

Issue #17. Entry: `navigation`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/navigation` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/navigation` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Tabs` | `label`, `items`, `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange`. Items include panel content and optional `disabled`. |
| `Navigation` | Web links use `href`; native destinations use host callbacks. |
| `Search` | `query`, `results`, `loading`, and `error`. The host supplies the search index and router. |

## When to use and examples

Do: expose current location and keep deep-link ownership with host. Don’t: replace native back with a browser history dependency.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Tabs use selected states and one active panel; DOM Arrow/Home/End keys, RTL-aware arrow mapping. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order. The active DOM panel is a tab stop only when its first content is not focusable. When the panel starts with a focusable element, such as the `InstallCommand` `pre`, that element is the single stop after the tab list. Panels that start with text keep `tabIndex=0` so their content stays reachable. Server and hydration markup render every panel with `tabIndex=0`; on the client a layout effect corrects the shown panel before paint, in the same commit that shows it, so a panel that starts with a focusable element is never an extra stop after a tab switch. Accordion uses details/summary on DOM and expanded Pressable on RN. Search results are visible action lists; keyboard shortcuts belong to host.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Breadcrumb is DOM-specific; native host routes plus BackButton are supported alternatives. No fuzzy-search engine, command palette shortcut hijacking or native hardware-keyboard certification.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Overlays · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/overlays.md

# Overlays · HIG 0.1.0

Dialogs, sheets, menus, and contextual help with explicit dismissal and focus behavior.

Includes `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Sheet`, and `Menu`. `Popover` and `Tooltip` are web-only; native help uses persistent `HelpText`.

Issue #16. Entry: `overlay`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/overlay` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/overlay` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | Controlled `open` and `onOpenChange`, plus `title`, `description`, and `children`. The web `trigger` is one element that accepts a ref. `closeLabel` overrides the Close button (`Sheet`, web `Popover`, native `Menu` and `GestureSheet` too); web `AlertDialog` takes `cancelLabel`. Defaults come from HIGProvider [`messages`](../foundations/localization.md#built-in-component-strings). |
| Web host composition | `title` remains required; `titleHidden` keeps its accessible name when the host renders a visible heading in the card. `description` is optional; `descriptionHidden` keeps supplied supporting text available to assistive technology. `contentRef` reaches the actual modal element. `contentProps` accepts layout classes/styles, DOM attributes and Radix focus/Escape/outside events; HIG retains ownership of the dialog id, role, naming associations, locale, direction, children and mounting behavior. Owned props and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` are filtered at runtime for JavaScript callers too; the caller's object is left unchanged. |
| Web close control | Omit `closeButton` for the current translated action, pass a ref-capable button element for a custom control, or pass `null` when the host supplies its own explicit dismissal action. Custom controls are composed with Radix Close; disabled buttons and `event.preventDefault()` retain their normal behavior. `closeLabel`/`cancelLabel` label only the default action. |
| Optional web `GestureSheet` | A separate Vaul modal root owns real drag, snap points, scroll handoff and focus scope. The Dialog title/description, trigger, close control and `contentRef` contracts apply. `backendProps` retains typed Vaul flags and snap-point options; `contentProps` retains host layout, DOM data attributes, focus/Escape/outside events and pointer capture events. `handleProps`/`handleRef` customize the actual backend handle; `handle={false}` omits it. `overlayProps` observes outside-pointer actions or retains host overlay styling. |
| Native focus targets | `initialFocusRef` and `returnFocusRef` accept live focus targets. Initial focus defaults to the title; the host supplies the trigger ref (Menu and Select pass their own trigger). |
| `Menu` | `label` and items with `label`, optional `disabled`, and `onSelect`. |
| Optional native `GestureSheet` | `contentMode='default'` scrolls the title, optional description, children and Close action. `contentMode='custom'` provides an unpadded, full-height content container; the host owns its header, back/close actions, safe-area content padding and scrolling. `title` remains required as the accessible name. Pass `titleRef` attached to the caller's accessible heading to focus it on open; without it, the sheet focuses its visually hidden title. |

Native `Dialog` and its aliases support `contentMode='custom'`: host content/actions, required `title`, one HIG Modal owning Back, accessibility escape and focus. `titleRef` targets the host heading (otherwise hidden); `initialFocusRef` overrides it, `returnFocusRef` targets the trigger. Rejected close retains focus.

`stageComponent` accepts `GestureHandlerRootView`; `stageStyle`/`stageTestID` configure it. `backdrop` supplies the scrim/action; `contentStyle`/`testID` configure the surface. Preserve accessible descendants and close policy; never nest Modals.

`animationType` defaults to `none`; reduced motion forces `none`. Animated iOS focus return waits for [iOS-only `onDismiss`](https://reactnative.dev/docs/modal#ondismiss); Android restores next frame. Keep mounted with `open={false}` through dismissal. Reopen/unmount cancels restoration.

A web card can keep its own visible heading and close geometry without replacing the modal's focus scope:

```tsx
<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(next) => {
    if (!next && pending) return;
    setOpen(next);
  }}
  title={t('reviewTitle')}
  titleHidden
  description={t('reviewDescription')}
  descriptionHidden
  contentRef={panelRef}
  contentProps={{ className: 'host-review-card', style: { maxWidth: 420 } }}
  closeButton={<button type='button' disabled={pending} aria-label={t('close')}>×</button>}
>
  <h2>{t('reviewTitle')}</h2>
  {reviewContent}
</Dialog>
```

Here `t`, `panelRef`, the card content and pending state belong to the host. The visible heading remains a real heading; the hidden Radix title supplies the modal's accessible name. An omitted description removes its ARIA association instead of referencing a missing element. `contentProps.onOpenAutoFocus` and `onCloseAutoFocus` can prevent the default focus choice; the host then supplies the intended focus target. Other content events retain Radix cancellation semantics. Controlled `onOpenChange` can reject a pending wallet close without unmounting the dialog or moving focus back to the trigger. `AlertDialog` continues to prevent outside-pointer dismissal even when a host observes that event.

These web composition props apply to `Dialog`, `AlertDialog` and the static `Sheet` alias. They do not add drag gestures, detents or product keyboard heuristics to the static sheet.

For a native card stack, import `GestureSheet` from `@bloxwap/hig-native/gesture-sheet` and render the caller's cards directly:

```tsx
const titleRef = useRef<Text>(null);

<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title={card.title}
  titleRef={titleRef}
  contentMode='custom'
  snapPoints={card.snapPoints}
  returnFocusRef={triggerRef}
>
  <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
    <Heading ref={titleRef}>{card.title}</Heading>
    {card.content}
    <Button onPress={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</Button>
  </View>
</GestureSheet>
```

Here `Text` and `View` are React Native types/components, and the host supplies the card state and its own accessible back/close labels. Custom content can use its own Gorhom scrollable or list without an outer scroll view. `snapPoints` may change while open: the current detent index is retained, or clamped to the highest remaining index if its detent was removed. Detent changes keep the sheet mounted and do not repeat open focus. Keep at least one sorted snap point; `initialIndex` applies to the next presentation. Focus return, Android Back, reduced-motion and dismissible backdrop behavior apply in both content modes.

For content-sized native cards, set `enableDynamicSizing` and omit `snapPoints`. This chooses one backend-measured detent rather than adding a competing fixed point. In custom mode HIG uses Gorhom's `BottomSheetView` to report intrinsic layout; it keeps a plain full-height `View` in fixed mode so nested scrollable registration stays with the caller. Choose the sizing mode for the presentation and avoid `flex: 1` or a full-height constraint on content that should determine its own height. Bound a long card's own scroll view. Default anatomy continues to use the backend scroll view. Mixed headers/footers and nested registered Gorhom scrollables compete for the backend's content-height measurement: their scroll content can replace the whole card height. Use host-measured fixed snap points for that composition. A content-sized card can instead bound a plain React Native `ScrollView` and set `enableContentPanningGesture={false}`, retaining the handle gesture and its own scroll gesture. This follows [Gorhom dynamic sizing](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/dynamic-sizing).

```tsx
<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title='Size and leverage'
  contentMode='custom'
  enableDynamicSizing
  maxDynamicContentSize={availableHeight}
>
  <View>{contentSizedCard}</View>
</GestureSheet>
```

`maxDynamicContentSize` is an optional finite positive ceiling in native points; the backend container height is the default. The dynamic detent uses index `0`. Changing content or the ceiling keeps the presentation and card state; height updates do not repeat open focus. A fixed sheet still requires a nonempty `snapPoints` list. `enableContentPanningGesture` passes through to the backend, allowing hosts with an independently scrolling list to disable content panning without changing their close/Back actions.

Host card stacks may also supply `onDismiss` to clear retained card state only after an accepted close settles. Rejected closes and interrupted reopenings do not call it. `onHardwareBackPress` can consume Android Back (`true`) or defer to the host's nested-card dispatcher (`false`); omitting it keeps the default dismissal behavior.

`topInset` and `bottomInset` default to safe-area values; use `0` for an intentional flush edge. `handleComponent` (including `null` for an overlay handle), `handleStyle`, `handleIndicatorStyle`, `backgroundComponent` and `backgroundStyle` retain host geometry and decoration. The backend measures the rendered handle. Use `useColors()` in custom backgrounds. `modalRef` exposes the optional backend's imperative motion methods; hosts must keep controlled `open` in sync with `present()`/`dismiss()`. Focus return and settled `onDismiss` remain controlled by the HIG wrapper. `animateOnMount`, `animationConfigs` and `backdropComponent` retain host entry motion and backdrop styling; the reduced-motion mapping still applies. A custom backdrop must honor the host dismissal policy.

Keyboard policies are typed backend options: `keyboardBehavior`, `keyboardBlurBehavior` and `android_keyboardInputMode`. Defaults remain HIG's `interactive`, `restore` and `adjustResize`. A host retaining an existing Gorhom policy can explicitly pass `none` for blur and `adjustPan` on Android. See [Gorhom keyboard handling](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/keyboard-handling).

For a screen-level drawer that must prepare and retain its native children while closed, choose `presentation='inline'`. HIG uses the public persistent `BottomSheet` backend; the default remains `presentation='modal'` with `BottomSheetModal`. Inline content stays mounted at index `-1`, hidden from accessibility and touch, and registers no Back listener while closed. Opening and reopening keep child/controller/list state. Rejected closes restore the last open detent; accepted closes return focus and call `onDismiss` once after settling. Use `sheetRef` for the inline backend's actual `expand`, `close` and `snapToIndex` methods; `modalRef` is only available in modal mode and exposes `present`/`dismiss`. Imperative calls must keep controlled `open` in sync. `onChange` observes backend index/position/type after HIG updates its index, focus and close request; it cannot replace those handlers. This lets a host change its animation policy after the opening detent settles. `containerStyle` retains sibling overlay order. Hosts own screen-level backdrop/container layering for inline presentation. No modal portal provider is required for inline sheets.

## Optional web gesture backend

Install `vaul ^1.1.2` and import `GestureSheet` from `@bloxwap/hig-react/gesture-sheet`. Core `overlay`, Button and overlay-free recipes do not import or install Vaul. The backend supplies its own motion CSS when loaded; HIG's explicitly imported component CSS supplies scoped surface, text, geometry and reduced-motion rules. See the official [Vaul anatomy and API](https://vaul.emilkowal.ski/api) and the verified [1.1.2 source](https://github.com/emilkowalski/vaul/blob/v1.1.2/src/index.tsx).

```tsx
import {GestureSheet} from '@bloxwap/hig-react/gesture-sheet';

<GestureSheet
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(next) => { if (next || !pending) setOpen(next); }}
  title={t('markets')}
  titleHidden
  contentMode='custom'
  contentRef={panelRef}
  contentProps={{ className: 'host-market-card', style: { bottom: viewportBottom, maxHeight: availableHeight } }}
  backendProps={{ handleOnly: false, repositionInputs: false, shouldScaleBackground: true, dismissible: !pending }}
  handleProps={{ style: { width: 100 }, preventCycle: true }}
  closeButton={null}
>
  <h2>{t('markets')}</h2>
  {hostHeaderAndScrollableContent}
</GestureSheet>
```

`contentMode='default'` provides padded, scrolling anatomy. `custom` leaves padding and scrolling with the host. The required accessible title remains available when hidden; render a real visible heading when the host card needs one. `closeButton={null}` means the host must retain an explicit accessible close/Back action. `handleOnly=true` requires the actual handle for dragging. Handle styles, classes and capture events are customizable; HIG filters replacements for the backend's handle pointer/click handlers, hidden state and reserved `data-vaul-*` attributes. Frozen caller prop objects remain unchanged.

Backend defaults remain Vaul's: `handleOnly=false`, `repositionInputs=true`, `shouldScaleBackground=false`, `dismissible=true` and `autoFocus=false`. Retain existing host flags explicitly. With `autoFocus=false`, hosts may use `contentProps.onOpenAutoFocus` to focus their heading/search control without requesting a software keyboard automatically. `shouldScaleBackground=true` requires the host's `[data-vaul-drawer-wrapper]` around the page. Physical `backendProps.direction` is independent of the provider's text direction. Snap points retain Vaul's viewport geometry; a full-height snapping panel should supply its own full-height layout. The modal root stays controlled and modal; there is no second nested HIG Dialog root.

The host can reject `onOpenChange(false)` while pending; HIG restores Vaul's last resting motion styles after a rejected drag without remounting card state. Use `dismissible=false` as well when pending should prevent dismissal attempts altogether. Backend `onAnimationEnd` is observed only when its reported state still matches controlled `open`, so rejected closes and stale opposite-state callbacks cannot clear retained card state. Programmatic state changes keep the backend's callback behavior. Reduced motion removes the sheet/overlay animation and transition; drag and snap selection still work. Viewport measurements, editable-input blur policy, animated content-height utilities, safe-area padding and product-specific keyboard accessory reserves stay in the host.

`scripts/gesture-sheet-browser-smoke.mjs` exercises the real Vaul backend in Chromium and WebKit: drag/scroll handoff, handle-only drag, controlled veto with retained input identity, nondismissible state, snap expansion, focus trap/Escape/return, viewport resizing, host styles/refs and reduced motion. Evidence in `evidence/web-gesture-sheet/` records the exact source baseline and dirty state. Desktop viewport resizing does not certify physical mobile software-keyboard behavior; that remains a host/device observation.

## When to use and examples

Do: repeat the order amount and give an explicit cancel action. Don’t: hide essential terms in hover help or execute confirm on open.

## States, interaction and accessibility

DOM Radix focus scopes restore trigger focus, trap modal focus, handle Escape and scroll locks. AlertDialog blocks outside-click dismissal. Menus use roving keyboard focus. Native Modal owns back and keyboard avoidance with scrollable content. Native overlays follow the host orientation: React Native's iOS Modal defaults `supportedOrientations` to portrait, so HIG passes every orientation and opening a Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Menu or Select never rotates a landscape host back to portrait (observed on the iOS Simulator, `evidence/native-sim/ios/orientation/`). Hosts still decide which orientations the app supports.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Basic Sheet uses static Modal layout. The separate optional `@bloxwap/hig-native/gesture-sheet` entry provides GestureSheet with sorted snapPoints, initialIndex, dismissible, safe-area/keyboard configuration, reduced-motion mapping, native back, scoped listener cleanup and controlled dismissal deduplication. Rejected controlled closes re-present after host state settles. See `fixtures/native/gesture-sheet.tsx` and `index-gesture.js` for the real separate consumer; packed smoke compiles both Android/iOS entry points. Hosts provide GestureHandlerRootView, SafeAreaProvider and BottomSheetModalProvider. Required optional peers are Gorhom 5.2.14, Reanimated 4.1.1, Worklets 0.5.1 and Gesture Handler 2.28.0, pinned to Expo 54 bundledNativeModules rather than the newer monorepo native runtime. Backend configuration follows [Gorhom usage](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/modal/usage) and [props](https://gorhom.dev/react-native-bottom-sheet/props). Mocked wiring and Metro compilation are not gesture-detent or TalkBack certification. With TalkBack on the Android emulator, opening Dialog/AlertDialog/Sheet/Menu moves accessibility focus to the heading and Back closes the overlay; without a `returnFocusRef` TalkBack falls back to the first screen element, so hosts should pass the trigger. VoiceOver does not run in the iOS Simulator, so VoiceOver focus restoration remains a physical-device observation (`evidence/native-sim/`). Native help is persistent text; no hover tooltip or anchored popover claim.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Recipes · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/recipes.md

# Recipes · HIG 0.1.0

Composed patterns for balances, markets, trade review, and documentation.

Includes `MarketRow`, `BalanceCard`, `TradeEntry`, `ActivityList`, `InstallCommand`, `CodeWindow`, and `MarketingHero`.

Issue #26. Entry: `recipes`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/recipes` according to applicability below. On web, each recipe also has its own entry, for example `@bloxwap/hig-react/recipes/install-command`, `recipes/code-window`, `recipes/market-row`, `recipes/balance-card`, `recipes/marketing-hero` and `recipes/activity-list`. These need no Radix peer; `smoke:packed-boundaries` renders and bundles them with no Radix installed (#63). `recipes/trade-entry` and the aggregate `recipes` entry need `@radix-ui/react-dialog` for the confirm step. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

All data and actions are supplied by the host application.

| Recipe | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `TradeEntry` | Raw `amount`, `onAmountChange`, `onConfirm`, `available`, `busy`, and `error`; opens review before submission. |
| `InstallCommand` | `command` and `onCopy`; accepts an asynchronous host clipboard adapter. |
| `MarketRow` (web) | `symbol`, `name`, `price`, `change`, and `onSelect`; `priceOptions` controls Intl precision and currency/decimal presentation; `changeOptions` controls percent-point precision/signs. `mode='presentation'` lets a host option own selection, with optional `identity`, `icon`, `favorite`, and formatted `volume` slots. |

Web `MarketRow` keeps its name button and USD formatting by default. A command palette that already owns option selection uses presentation mode to avoid a second action and tab stop:

```tsx
<CommandItem onSelect={()=>openMarket(market.symbol)}>
  <MarketRow mode='presentation' symbol={market.symbol} name={market.name}
    price={market.price} priceOptions={{style:'decimal',maximumFractionDigits:8}}
    change={market.change} changeOptions={{minimumFractionDigits:2,maximumFractionDigits:2}}
    identity={<><strong>{market.symbol}</strong> {market.name}</>} icon={<MarketIcon symbol={market.symbol}/>}
    favorite={<FavoriteIndicator selected={market.favorite}/>}
    volume={<NumberReadout value={market.volume} options={{notation:'compact'}}/>}
    style={{gridTemplateColumns:'minmax(0,1fr) 12ch 8ch 10ch'}}/>
</CommandItem>
```

Presentation mode uses a grid with logical numeric alignment and no block padding. The host can set matching column widths on each row through `style`/`className`, its compact height and the surrounding keyboard/option semantics. The number face inherits from that row. Slots render host content; keep decorative icons/indicators hidden from assistive technology, or give interactive controls their own names and deliberate keyboard behavior. Presentation rows accept no `onSelect` and emit no action feedback. Tiny prices keep the requested precision; unknown values remain —. Volume formatting and units stay host-owned. The optional `identity` slot belongs to presentation mode; action mode keeps its named HIG button. Hosts that use `toFixed` rounding should pass their already-rounded percent-point value plus explicit `changeOptions` to preserve binary rounding, trailing digits, signs and negative zero. Options use the same contract as `Percent`: the input is percent points, and the rendered style remains percent.

## When to use and examples

Do: compose primitives and explicit outcomes in comfortable app or compact Pro context. Don’t: put wallet/network/SDK services in core packages.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Native CodeWindow and InstallCommand render code in the provider's `monoFontFamily` (for example the registered `BloxwapMonoRegular`; platform monospace otherwise) and keep code left-to-right inside RTL roots. Copy failures leave a manual-selection recovery message. Trade confirm remains host-controlled; no demo sends a transaction. Web/native fixtures show balance, market, entry and feedback preference previews.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

M2 supplies visual recipes; M3 adds semantic feedback composition because #26 depends on #25. Product visual fidelity is provisional until inaccessible monorepo audit. Account/positions variants can compose these primitives without service coupling.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/pro-data.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/pro-data-typecheck.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. ## Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/selection.md

# Selection controls · HIG 0.1.0

Controls for choosing options, changing preferences, and adjusting values.

Includes `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, and `Slider`. See the navigation guide for `Tabs`.

Issue #15. Entry: `selection`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/selection` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/selection` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Control | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Checkbox and switch | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, and `onCheckedChange`. Native `Switch` also takes `tone`, a token role (`action` default, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, `info`, `buy`, `sell`) for the on track; raw colours are not accepted and fall back to `action`. On Android the thumb uses the `text` token, so the app theme accent never shows. |
| Choice controls | `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange`. Options have `value`, `label`, and optional `disabled`. Native options also accept `description` (a second line) and `lang` (the label's BCP-47 language). |
| `Slider` | `min`, `max`, `step`, and `value`; a visible `label` is required. The DOM keyboard focus ring is drawn inside the 48px range box, so it never paints over the label or the next control at comfortable or compact density. Native increment/decrement actions use HIGProvider `messages.increase`/`messages.decrease`. |

## When to use and examples

Do: control selection from accepted host state. Don’t: emit a success cue on every render or repeated slider value.

Native language pickers can keep the native name and a translated description in one radio row:

```tsx
<HIGProvider locale='en-US' fontFamiliesByScript={{
  latin: {400: 'BloxwapSansRegular'},
  ko: {400: 'BloxwapSansKRRegular'},
  zh: {400: 'BloxwapSansSCRegular'},
}}>
  <RadioGroup label='Language' value={language} onValueChange={setLanguage} options={[
    {value: 'ko', label: '한국어', description: 'Korean', lang: 'ko-KR'},
    {value: 'zh', label: '简体中文', description: 'Chinese', lang: 'zh-Hans'},
  ]}/>
</HIGProvider>
```

Register each face before passing its name. `Text` chooses `fontFamiliesByScript` by the label's glyphs, independently of the app locale; `lang` supplies `accessibilityLanguage` and resolves shared CJK punctuation. Descriptions use the app language. A script map selects the requested static weight, or its nearest registered weight; the existing `fontFamilies`/`fontFamily` remain the fallback. Explicit text `script` and style `fontFamily` override detection and registered family selection respectively. Native radios expose the label, supporting description as an accessibility hint, checked/disabled state and the explicit `activate` accessibility action; disabled rows reject both touch and accessibility activation. Per-option language is passed to React Native's `accessibilityLanguage`; pronunciation support depends on the platform and installed voices.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Native HTML controls retain browser keyboard and selection semantics. RN Switch renders the OS track inside one labeled 48dp switch row (the row is the accessibility element and touch target); checkbox/radio use labeled Pressables with checked state. RN slider uses the optional community backend for the visual track and touch drag; a plain 48dp adjustable View owns the label, value and increment/decrement actions (5% steps) on iOS and Android because the backend's iOS Fabric view ignores accessibility increments and its Android SeekBar node measures 18dp. On Android the wrapper is the package's autolinked `HIGAdjustableView`, which also lists `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` for Voice Access and Switch Access: a requested value snaps to `step`, clamps to `min`/`max`, updates the control once and is rejected while disabled. React Native's own `accessibilityActions` cannot express set-progress (custom names get synthetic ids and the progress argument is dropped). Without native linking (Expo Go) the wrapper is a plain View and set-progress is absent. The backend's native track height (18dp Android, 40pt iOS) still bounds direct touch drag; hosts needing a larger drag area should pad around the control. Select opens labeled native Modal choices and returns focus to its trigger.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

SegmentedControl is single-choice radio semantics, not navigation. Native picker alternative is deliberate. Accessibility increment/decrement, set-progress and disabled rejection are verified on the iOS Simulator and Android emulator (`evidence/native-sim/`); tactile drag feel and haptic rate remain physical-device work; backend is an optional native peer.

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, `tests/native/language-options.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.

`SwitchRow` from `@bloxwap/hig-native/switch` (also `selection`) wraps an existing host row in one switch target. It takes the same required `label`, `checked` / `defaultChecked`, `disabled` and `onCheckedChange` contract as `Switch`, plus required noninteractive `children` and root Pressable props. Keep the visible label, description and track noninteractive: the root owns activation and hides the content from accessibility to avoid duplicate targets. Put the description in `accessibilityHint`. Root `style` supports pressed callbacks; `accessibilityState` preserves `busy` while HIG owns checked/disabled state. Disable the row explicitly during pending requests; busy alone is descriptive. The Expo web row supports Space, Enter and pointer activation. Tree shaking an ESM import of ordinary `Switch` removes this optional anatomy.


## Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/components/status.md

# Status & feedback · HIG 0.1.0

Visible progress, notifications, and recoverable states that keep people informed.

Includes `Badge`, `Alert`, `Callout`, `Toast`, `Progress`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `Avatar`, and `StatusIndicator`.

Issue #18. Entry: `status`. Import platform entries from `@bloxwap/hig-react/status` or `@bloxwap/hig-native/status` according to applicability below. Import `@bloxwap/hig-react/css` once on web; tokens CSS is a separate explicit import.

## API and anatomy

| Component | Key props and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Badge` | Quiet label; web adds explicit `tone` (`neutral`, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, or `info`), standard span props and a forwarded span ref. The neutral default retains its appearance. Tone uses provider token roles and never infers meaning from text or a number's sign. Badge adds no live region; the host owns announcements. |
| `Alert` | `title`, `severity`, and an optional recovery `action`. Severity sets the accent edge from a token role on web and native: info → `info`, success → `positive`, warning → `warning`, error → `negative`. On native, `tone` swaps in another token role for an approved product accent, never a raw colour. |
| `Callout` | Same API as `Alert`, for static guidance. It adds the documentation severities `note` (`info` role) and `tip` (`positive` role), so SDK docs do not need their own edge colours. Pass `announce={false}` for callouts present at page load. `title` accepts a ReactNode, such as text with a `<code>` span; on web it renders inside `<strong>` and should stay inline. On native it renders inside the `Heading`, so pass a string or inline `Text`; its visible text is announced. |
| `Toast` | `notices` with stable `id`, `message`, `severity`, and optional `action`; `onDismiss` handles dismissal. Native notices also accept `description` and `closable` (default true when `onDismiss` is supplied). Native `maxHeight` bounds a scrolling viewport; it defaults to 60% of the window height and accepts dp or a parent percentage. `dismissLabel` overrides visible Dismiss text; its accessible name contains that text. |
| `Progress` | `label`, `value`, and `max`. |
| `EmptyState` | `title`, `description`, and an optional `action`. |

Native `EmptyState` keeps the default `Surface`, `Heading` and body-text anatomy. Its `description` is optional; omitted or empty text leaves no blank description node. Pass decorative `illustration` content before the heading; HIG hides the whole illustration subtree from VoiceOver/TalkBack navigation while keeping the heading and action accessible. The host controls the illustration's dimensions and spacing. Root `ViewProps`, including `style`, `testID` and layout events, pass to the Surface. `titleStyle` and `descriptionStyle` reach the actual text nodes; `maxFontSizeMultiplier` caps both, or inherits the provider policy when omitted. Text keeps the provider palette and heading semantics unless the host explicitly styles it.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  title={t('noMarkets')}
  illustration={<BrandMark width={64} height={64} />}
  style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', backgroundColor: 'transparent', padding: 0, gap: 12 }}
  titleStyle={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 28, textAlign: 'center' }}
  maxFontSizeMultiplier={2}
  action={<Button onPress={clearFilters}>{t('browseAll')}</Button>}
/>
```

The mark and clear-filter action remain host-owned. `tests/native/empty-state.test.cjs` verifies default anatomy, omitted descriptions, decorative accessibility metadata, real text/root props and accepted action delivery; these wiring checks are not physical-device accessibility certification.

## When to use and examples

Do: keep critical failure inline with Retry; use toast for copied acknowledgement. Don’t: dismiss critical text on a timer or rely on audio for success.

## States, interaction and accessibility

Notifications deduplicate ids and preserve every message until explicit dismissal, including bursts larger than three. Host delivery queues may limit arrivals, but the renderer never silently removes an undismissed message. A single coalesced announcement reports each changed burst, prioritizing errors; unchanged rerenders do not repeat it. DOM and Expo web use one live region while every notification remains visible. Native Android uses explicit announcement delivery, and inline Android status uses live-region metadata; iOS announces changed inline content explicitly. Actual VoiceOver/TalkBack timing remains unobserved. Skeleton and spinner are static under candidate motion policy.

State review: rest; keyboard focus/hover (DOM); accepted press and release/cancel; selected/checked where applicable; disabled; busy; inline error/recovery; empty/loading; long translations/large text; reduced motion; sound and haptics disabled. No host action occurs on mere focus. Disabled/busy targets suppress accepted activation. Core has no required feedback backend; the optional provider callback follows the action, honors cancellation and isolates errors.

## Platform mapping and limits

Toast is an inline notification stack, no mandatory portal/timer backend. Host owns delivery ordering/persistence. On native, messages use body-size semibold text and descriptions use a separate body-size line; neither truncates or disables text scaling. The stack scrolls within `maxHeight`, including nested host scroll views. A notice with `closable={false}` has no Dismiss action; host recovery actions remain available. Without `onDismiss`, notices have no Dismiss buttons. No notice expires automatically: remove it from the controlled `notices` array when its host lifetime ends; keep failures with recovery actions until explicitly resolved. VoiceOver/TalkBack observations are pending, automated role/state tests are not device evidence.

```tsx
// Native: compact notices with large-text scrolling and a persistent failure.
<Toast
  maxHeight={320}
  notices={[
    { id: 'saved', message: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are ready.', severity: 'success' },
    { id: 'retry', message: 'Transfer failed', description: 'Check your balance and retry.', severity: 'error', closable: false },
  ]}
  onDismiss={removeNotice}
/>
```

## Validation and citation

See `tests/components.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/native/components.test.cjs`, consumer fixtures and milestone evidence. Physical hardware, assistive-technology and baseline product comparisons are unperformed unless linked explicitly. Cite HIG 0.1.0 with this chapter anchor and a commit permalink, not a mutable preview branch. Preserve business behavior behind a host rollback flag during adoption.


## Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0
Source: docs/feedback/adapters.md

# Optional adapters and installation · HIG 0.1.0

Issues #22–#24. Base imports do not load adapters. Individual `web-sound`, `browser-haptic`, `web-haptic`, `native` and `react` entries preserve dependency boundaries. The composite `web` entry needs the Haptic package; sound-only consumers should import `web-sound`.

## Web sound

Install `@bloxwap/hig-feedback@0.1.0 @bloxwap/sfx@0.1.0`. `createWebSoundAdapter()` loads SFX only for enabled requests after an accepted interaction. It calls the documented unlock/play APIs, passes per-call volume and uses the same presets as native. New requests replace pending startup, so delayed loading does not create a backlog. It avoids upstream global enabled/volume stores because HIG preferences are root-scoped. `@bloxwap/sfx/react` owns global preference helpers; using those alongside HIG would create competing preference owners.

HIG passes one adapter-local `AbortSignal` to each play. Muting, backgrounding, explicit cancellation and disposal abort that root's plays; the next accepted request gets a fresh signal. With the engine merged in [sfx#51](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/pull/51), this stops buffered and live voices while other roots and host-owned voices continue. Generations still discard superseded startup/unlock requests. HIG reference-counts default adapters and disposes the shared engine after the last user. A host that also owns that engine should inject/own its lifecycle.

**Released compatibility:** published `@bloxwap/sfx@0.1.0` ignores the additional signal option. It remains compatible, and cancellation still prevents pending HIG playback, but its already-running voices continue. The signal-aware engine exists in merged source, not an npm release yet. Active-voice cancellation is forward-ready source support; released adoption remains pending in #70. No global `stopAll()` workaround is used.

## Browser and physical-tap haptics

`createBrowserHapticAdapter()` maps accepted semantic events to browser vibration when `navigator.vibrate` exists. Its existing default and `{vibrate}` injection retain their patterns and work with published `@bloxwap/haptic@0.1.0`; neither imports Haptic. Device intensity/pattern quality varies and may be suppressed. iOS WebKit without vibration cannot provide imperative async outcome feedback; the adapter reports unavailable and remains silent.

The optional `ImperativeHapticBackend` injection accepts the exact `canTriggerHaptic` and `triggerHaptic` functions merged in [haptic#30](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/pull/30): `createBrowserHapticAdapter({canTriggerHaptic, triggerHaptic})`. These exports are absent from published `0.1.0`; use the injection only with a host-owned source build until they ship. HIG probes capability at request time, so activation and document visibility are current, and delegates the semantic cue to upstream's presets. Rejection/failure cannot change the primary action. `observed` stays false. The adapter adds no eager import, helper DOM or physical-tap simulation.

The merged imperative API still reports iOS unavailable, including during transient activation. It cannot replace eligible physical targets or express iOS async outcome patterns. Neither the browser Vibration API nor this upstream API provides a per-root cancellation handle: `cancel()`/`dispose()` retain the existing `navigator.vibrate(0)` stop when available, which is document-wide. This is distinct from SFX's per-root voice cancellation.

For approved iOS physical action targets, install `@bloxwap/haptic@0.1.0` and wrap a single ref-capable HIG button in `HapticFeedbackTarget eligible`. The wrapper uses upstream `HapticTarget`, preserves the target/handler/ref, enables only the physical-tap route and disables debug audio/helper switch visibility. Thus browser vibration comes from the semantic adapter and is not duplicated by the wrapper. HIG preferences still gate the wrapper.

**Do** pre-approve the target with `eligible` after disabled/busy/policy checks. **Don't** wrap an action whose eligibility is decided only by an async click callback, or promise a programmable iOS success/error pattern. The OS physical tick occurs before delegated handlers; a later preventDefault cannot retract that tick. That cancellation limitation, physical-tap intensity limits and device/VoiceOver checks remain upstream [haptic#9](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/9) / [haptic#7](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/7). The missing imperative iOS API for semantic controllers is [haptic#27](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/27) (tracked in #70). No wrapper is required for basic actions.

## Native audio

Install the feedback package plus `expo-audio` (`~1.1.1` on Expo SDK 54, `~55.0.18` on SDK 55) only in the native host setup. `expoAudioBackend(Audio)` supplies a thin playback bridge; `createNativeSoundAdapter(backend, assets)` accepts Metro asset ids. The Expo gallery imports only the four committed WAV cues. Configure ambient/silent-mode behavior with `playsInSilentMode:false`, no background playback and `doNotMix` interruption mode. Host AppState calls `setBackground`; backgrounding pauses cached players. Call `preload()` at startup: it configures the audio session and caches players once. After that, `play()` dispatches synchronously, with no awaited bridge round trip before `player.play()`. It stops only the previous cue, issues `seekTo(0)` without awaiting it (native players apply calls in order) and plays. A cue requested before preload settles waits for it, and only the newest such request plays. Concurrency is limited to one active cue, volume/mute are honored, missing cues are silent, and disposal pauses/removes every cached player.

Playback completion: HIG does not listen to `playbackStatusUpdate` and never relies on `didJustFinish`. On Android, `expo-audio` 1.1 (Expo SDK 54) reports `didJustFinish` twice for one finished cue; SDK 55 (`expo-audio` 55.0) reports it once (#89). In the Android emulator run, SDK 54 had 4 `play()` calls, 4 playing starts and 8 `didJustFinish` statuses: the same finish reported twice, not a second play (`evidence/native-sim/issue-86-88-89/`). In `expo-audio` 1.1, every status sent while the player is ended carries `didJustFinish: true`, and two listeners send one when a cue ends. A host or future adapter that acts on completion must de-duplicate it, for example by ignoring a `didJustFinish` that has no `play()` or `playing: true` status since the last one. Device timing for both SDKs is tracked in #55.

Regenerate with `npm run generate:cues`. `assets/manifest.json` pins package/recipe/export flags, 48kHz mono PCM16, durations, peaks/RMS, bytes and reviewed hashes. Noise recipes vary; do not assert regenerated WAV bytes are deterministic. Inspect duration/envelope/level tolerances and review the actual artifact hashes. Offline generation dependencies are dev-only; Metro never imports them or browser synthesis.

## Native haptics

Install `expo-haptics` (`~15.0.7` on Expo SDK 54, `~55.0.18` on SDK 55) in the native host. `expoHapticBackend(Haptics)` bridges selection, impact light/medium/heavy and notification success/warning/error. `createNativeHapticAdapter` reports API availability separately from observation. Unsupported hardware, backgrounding, preferences and failed backend calls are no-ops that do not change primary actions. Android notification/impact approximation and OS suppression must be observed on devices before support is certified.

## Simulated lifecycle regression evidence

Pinned, unmodified MIT source fixtures from SFX `1be6630` and Haptic `8b1ab578` test the adapters against the merged implementations, with source hashes and licenses in `tests/fixtures/upstream-feedback/`.
